exposure: maternal anemia (categorized by hemoglobin levels: no anemia, mild, moderate, severe, or unspecified severity)
cohort: Pregnant women attending Sri Balaji Medical College Hospital and Research Institute in Tirupati, India, between January 2023 and January 2024.
finding: Maternal anemia was associated with increased maternal morbidity, including longer hospitalization, more antenatal admissions, preeclampsia, placenta previa, and higher rates of cesarean delivery, as well as increased perinatal morbidity and mortality, including preterm birth, small-for-gestational-age live birth, low Apgar scores, neonatal death, and perinatal death.
mod_finding: Rates of cesarean delivery were higher among women with anemia.
